lane: AdSense maximisation: page elements, ad formats, policy edges, payments and India for a sports-quiz duel on Cloudflare (extends lane-adtech.json; nothing there is repeated)
headline: The money on an AdSense-funded quiz site is made on two different surfaces that want opposite ad strategies, and Google's own policy text draws the line for us. The static, crawlable question/answer pages are ordinary content pages: Auto ads, in-content display units, a bottom anchor and a link-click vignette are all allowed there and Google's inventory-value policy is satisfied because there is more content than ads. The app shell (lobby, duel, receipt) is a game: the only Google unit that belongs there is the H5 Games Ads 'reward' placement, plus one display unit under a receipt that carries real content (score, answer review, fairness receipt), because Google forbids ads on screens 'used for alerts, navigation or other behavioral purposes' and H5 policy forbids full-screen ads that 'interrupt the user during periods of continuous game play'. Anchors and vignettes must never run in the shell: vignettes now fire on the browser back button and on '30 seconds of inactivity followed by user interaction' (triggers added 9 Feb 2026), which is exactly a quiz player's behaviour, and an anchor on a non-scrolling game screen sits over the controls. Reward copy may only describe the reward ('Watch an ad to earn 50 coins'); 'support us', 'click the ads', arrows and misleading images are the wording Google lists as violations, and rewarded inventory is the one explicit exception to the 'encouraging clicks' rule. Revenue expectations must be set on web-specific numbers, which disagree by 2x at the top (Playgama: US rewarded web $15-28 gross; AppLixir: tier-1 $6-15 gross, $4-8 take-home) and agree at the bottom (India/tier-3 $1-4 gross), with India display RPM in the Rs 40-165 band for entertainment content and 48% of Indian consumers saying they block ads. The account-level risks that end the business are not eCPM but (a) a 'low value content' refusal if we apply with an app shell instead of content pages, (b) invalid traffic from 'earn coins' communities behaving like paid-to-click, and (c) Cloudflare's bot protection blocking Google's ad crawler so ads.txt and site checks fail. Payments for an Indian individual are a USD wire from Google Asia Pacific (Singapore) converted by the receiving bank, $100 threshold, 21st-26th of the month, no Indian TDS; GST zero-rating needs an LUT.

findings.finding: H5 Games Ads is still by-application on top of an approved AdSense account and 'Account approval is not guaranteed as it is subject to partner eligibility.' No minimum traffic is published; the sign-up page only says to complete Google's form after the AdSense account is approved.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/1705831 read 2026-09-17: 'You need an approved AdSense account to show ads in your H5 games'; 'Account approval is not guaranteed as it is subject to partner eligibility.'

findings.finding: The H5 Games Ads placement policy (the page Google links from the sign-up) lists the exact full-screen placements that are banned and allowed. Banned: ads 'that might be confused with the normal operation of the application or hosting page', 'that are triggered after a user closes another full screen ad', 'that appear unexpectedly while a user is viewing the application or web page's content', 'that trigger after every user interaction', 'that interrupt the user during periods of continuous game play and heavy user interaction', 'that interfere with user navigation and interaction'. Allowed: ads 'that appear between screens of an application or content pages', 'at transitions between a games catalog and the individual games', and only ads 'created using the adBreak() function'. The page states no numeric frequency cap and no closability timer.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/9959170 read 2026-09-17; quoted verbatim.

findings.finding: Only one Ad Placement API placement type is rewarded: 'reward' ('The player reaches a point in the game where they can be offered a reward'). 'preroll', 'start', 'pause', 'next' and 'browse' are interstitials. 'There can only be one preroll placement in your game for each page load.' For a rewarded placement the API calls beforeReward(showAdFn) only when an ad is available, then adViewed or adDismissed; adBreakDone reports a breakStatus of notReady, timeout, invalid, error, noAdPreloaded, frequencyCapped ('An ad wasn't shown because the frequency cap was applied to this placement'), ignored ('The user didn't click on a reward prompt before they reached the next placement'), other, dismissed ('The user dismissed a rewarded ad before viewing it to completion') or viewed.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/ad-placement/docs/placement-types and /apis/adbreak read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Frequency is controlled by the script attribute data-ad-frequency-hint: 'Currently the default frequency is "120s" (i.e. ads show no more than once every 2 minutes on average)', 'the maximum rate that ads can show is once every 30s', 'The frequency control isn't applied to the very first ad placement (i.e. the first call to adBreak())', and it 'is a client side hint that could be ignored or overridden by a server control in future'. The page does not say whether the hint applies to 'reward' placements; the 2021 release notes (already in lane-adtech) recorded a bug where caps were wrongly applied to rewarded placements as resolved, which implies rewarded placements are meant to be exempt but this is not stated on the current page.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/ad-placement/docs/ad-rate read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: The Coalition for Better Ads standards (the ones Chrome enforces) for mobile web disallow: pop-up ads, prestitial ads, 'Ad Density Higher Than 30%', flashing animated ads, auto-playing video with sound, postitial ads with countdown, full-screen scrollover ads, large sticky ads, sticky pop-out video, and sticky video with a large inline ad. Desktop web adds 'Ad Density Higher than 50%' and 'Ad Density Higher Than 30% when Combined with a Sticky Video Ad'. The standards say nothing about games or rewarded ads; a rewarded video the user opted into is therefore judged as an ordinary ad experience if it is ever shown without the opt-in.
findings.evidence: betterads.org/standards read 2026-09-17. Chrome enforcement of these standards is well known but was not re-read for this lane.

findings.finding: Google Publisher Policies, 'Inventory value' (the current name of the 2016 'valuable inventory' rule): 'We do not allow Google-served ads on screens: without publisher-content or with low-value content, that are under construction, that are used for alerts, navigation or other behavioral purposes'; 'with embedded or copied content from others without additional commentary, curation, or otherwise adding value'; 'with more ads or other paid promotional material than publisher-content'. 'Out of context ads' bans ads 'in apps or web pages that run in the background, that appear outside the display, when the user's attention is expected to be elsewhere and not on the screen hosting the ad.' This is the clause that governs a results/receipt screen: it may carry a display unit only if it is a content screen (score breakdown, answer review, stats), not a transition or alert.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/10502938 read 2026-09-17, quoted verbatim.

findings.finding: The per-page ad-count limit was removed in August 2016 and replaced by the content-to-ad balance rule above; there is no numeric maximum of AdSense units per page today, only 'more ads than content' and the Better Ads density thresholds.
findings.evidence: martech.org and searchenginejournal.com reports of the 2016 change; the current policy text (10502938) contains no per-page count.

findings.finding: 'Encouraging clicks or views' is explicitly scoped to non-rewarded inventory: 'Except for rewarded inventory, publishers may not ask others to click or view their ads or use deceptive implementation methods to obtain clicks or views.' Prohibited examples: 'Compensating users for viewing ads or performing searches', 'Encouraging users to click the Google ads using phrases such as "click the ads", "support us", "visit these links" or other similar language', 'Directing user attention to the ads using arrows or other graphical gimmicks', 'Placing misleading images alongside individual ads'. Rewarded inventory is governed instead by 'Policies for ad units that offer rewards', which adds: 'Publishers must not include any text or icons, other than to describe the reward(s) offered, to mislead or incentivize users towards a particular choice (such as by indicating "watch this ad to support our business")' and 'Publishers must deliver the promised reward(s) to the user upon completion of the required action(s).' So the exact permitted wording is a plain description of the exchange ('Watch an ad to earn 50 coins'); 'support us', 'help keep the game free', 'click', arrows pointing at the unit and anything that steers the choice are the listed violations.
findings.evidence: Publisher Policies mirror at transparency.google (AdSense product terms embed) and support.google.com/adsense/answer/9121589, both read 2026-09-17; wording of the 'Encouraging clicks' section confirmed against the search snippet of support.google.com/publisherpolicies/answer/48182.

findings.finding: Invalid traffic as Google defines it includes 'Publishers encouraging clicks on their ads' alongside self-clicks, repeated clicks by a few users, and 'Automated clicking tools or traffic sources, robots, or other deceptive software'; 'ultimately it is your responsibility as the publisher to ensure that the traffic on your ads is valid.' The account-closure page adds: 'Publishers should not use third-party services that generate clicks or impressions such as paid-to-click, paid-to-surf, autosurf and click-exchange programs', 'Don't encourage or ask your friends, family, co-workers, etc. to click on your ads', and bans implementing ads 'in a way that they might be mistaken for other content, such as menu, navigation, or download links' and 'Manipulating the targeting of the ads to get higher revenue ads'. A rewarded ad that a user opted into is not incentivised *clicking*; an 'earn coins' community that farms rewarded views for multiple accounts is the same pattern as paid-to-surf and will be treated as IVT.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/16737 and /2660562 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Ad serving limits come in two named flavours, 'Account being assessed' (precautionary, while traffic quality is checked; typical for new accounts) and 'Invalid traffic concerns'; Google's stated cure is to keep building content, fix implementation and acquire traffic free of IVT risk. Practitioner data on deductions: 'fluctuations of 1%-5% in your AdSense earnings are normal and expected'; cases of 30%-70% deductions exist; clicks from data-centre IPs (which is what most VPN exits are) are more likely to be flagged.
findings.evidence: AdSense troubleshooter 12368721 (search summary; page itself not readable in full) and monetizemore.com IVT-deductions article (updated 18 Jan 2023).

findings.finding: Ad placement policy still carries the game-specific rule from the Flash era: 'When placing Google ads on Flash gaming sites, we strongly recommend a distance of at least 150 pixels between the ads and the edge of a game', because accidental clicks happen when users are concentrating on play. The same page bans ads in windows 'not initiated by an intentional user interaction', requires ad labels to be only 'Advertisements' or 'Sponsored Links', bans formatting ads to resemble navigation or download buttons, and bans refreshing 'a page or an element of a page without the user requesting a refresh'.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/1346295 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Auto ads today = overlay formats (anchor, vignette, side rails on widescreen) + in-page formats (banner, multiplex). Google 'will detect it, reanalyze your page and place ads' when the page changes, but there is no official AdSense document for single-page applications; the Auto ads 'ad load' control is now 'Use the slider to decide the maximum number of in-page ads to show on your pages' plus a 'Minimum distance between ads on a page' slider. Practitioner consensus for SPAs (Watmore; react-adsense issue #6) is to re-insert <ins> elements and call adsbygoogle.push({}) on each route change, and never to push twice into the same element ('already have ads' error). Re-rendering on a user-initiated route change is a new page view in spirit; re-rendering on a timer is the banned auto-refresh.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/9261805 and /9261806 read 2026-09-17; jasonwatmore.com SPA guide; github.com/hustcc/react-adsense/issues/6 (search summary). The refresh-on-route-change inference is mine, not Google's.

findings.finding: Vignette ads are 'full-screen ads that appear between page loads and can be skipped by users at any time'; the default trigger is a link click and the default frequency is 10 minutes, settable from 1 minute to 1 hour. Since 9 February 2026 the 'Allow additional triggers for vignette ads' control (on by default when vignettes are on) also fires vignettes when the user 'Reaches the end of a page's main article element and either they start scrolling back up, or 5 seconds elapse on mobile or 10 seconds on desktop', 'Is inactive for at least 30 seconds followed by user interaction', 'Navigates backward using their browser's back button (currently Chrome, Edge, and Opera)', unhides a tab, or opens a same-site page in a new tab. Every one of these is normal behaviour inside a quiz duel (thinking, then tapping; back-button navigation in an SPA), so vignettes cannot be enabled on any page that hosts the game shell.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/16531962, /13956167, /16853623 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Anchor ads 'stick to the edge of the user's screen and are easily dismissible. They appear when the user interacts with your page'; Google places them at the top unless that would hurt UX, top placement 'only appear[s] after scrolling down', and 'They're frequency capped per user on mobile to maintain a positive user experience.' Dynamic anchors can expand, collapse or dock in a corner. On a non-scrolling, full-viewport game screen an anchor therefore always lands at the bottom, over the answer controls, which is the H5 'interfere with user navigation and interaction' pattern.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/15484692 read 2026-09-17. Collapsible anchors on desktop from 21 May 2026 is from a search summary of AdSense announcements, not read at source.

findings.finding: Approval and setup: 'This usually takes a few days, but in some cases it can take 2-4 weeks'; 'Your site must be live and contain enough content for our specialists to evaluate'; the code goes 'between the <head> and </head> tags of a page that contains content'; 'You have 6 months to complete the steps to set up your account.' Site ownership can be shown by the AdSense code snippet, an ads.txt snippet in the root, or a meta tag (added for publishers who do not want ads on the homepage), and verification is now real time. AdSense then shows a 'last crawled' time and a 'Check for updates' button for ads.txt.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/76228 read 2026-09-17; ownership methods from searchenginejournal.com and support.google.com/adsense/answer/13996652 (search summary).

findings.finding: 'Low value content' is Google's catch-all refusal for new sites. Google publishes no minimum word or page count; practitioner reports converge on: original pages that answer a query, About/Contact/Privacy pages, HTTPS, a navigable site, pages indexed, and site age (one developer: 'Google wants 3-6 months of history before they trust you'). For a quiz site the specific exposure is the 'replicated content' clause: hundreds of near-identical per-question pages read as templated/thin. The cure is per-page substance (explanation, source, stats, related questions) and noindex on anything thinner.
findings.evidence: dev.to/bdubs rejection write-up; genieegroup.com and adstimate.com guides (2026); Google's own text is the 'Inventory value' clause above. Practitioner claims are unverified individually.

findings.finding: ads.txt for AdSense is one line, 'google.com, pub-0000000000000000, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0', 'uploaded to the root directory of your site'; 'It may take a few days for your changes to be reflected in AdSense. If your site doesn't make many ad requests it may take up to a month'; it is 'not mandatory, but it's highly recommended'. sellers.json: set 'Seller information visibility' to Transparent under Account > Settings; 'If your information isn't made transparent, advertisers won't be able to see your name, which might impact your revenue.'
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/7532444 and /9889911 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Cloudflare-specific hazard: Bot Fight Mode / Super Bot Fight Mode and high security levels challenge Google's ad crawlers (user agents Mediapartners-Google, Google-Display-Ads-Bot, AdsBot-Google), which shows up in AdSense as ads.txt 'not found', site 'down', or IVT flags. The fix used by publishers is a WAF custom rule that skips/allows those user agents (or the /ads.txt URI), then re-checking with the AdSense crawler tester. Cloudflare's own bot directory lists Mediapartners-Google as a verified bot.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/thread/410063384; community.cloudflare.com/t/bot-fight-mode-is-blocking-the-google-display-ads-bot/824648; techiesdiary.com fix; radar.cloudflare.com/bots/directory/googlemedia (all search summaries).

findings.finding: Payments: threshold '$100 USD or the currency equivalent'; 'If your current balance reaches the payment threshold by the end of the month, and there are no other payment holds, you'll be issued a payment between the 21st and the 26th of the month.' Address PIN: 'It usually takes 3 weeks for your PIN mail to arrive' (another page says 2-3 weeks); 'If you enter your PIN incorrectly 3 times, your account will stop showing ads'; 'You'll have 4 months from the date your PIN is generated to complete address verification'; identity verification, where asked, has a 45-day window; the PIN threshold 'can vary depending on your location' (the commonly cited $10 is not on the page). On cancellation the final payment arrives 'within approximately 90 days of the end of the month'.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/1709871, /157667, /1709858 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: India payment mechanics: the contracting entity for Asia-Pacific publishers is Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd., Singapore (GST reg 200817984R). Payment to an Indian bank is a USD international wire; 'Google pays most fees' and 'your bank may charge you a small fee' for the conversion; the receiving bank converts to INR (some banks require the purpose code P1007 'Advertising, trade fair, market research and public opinion polling services'); SWIFT code is mandatory; the wire reaches the bank within about 72 hours of 'Payment in progress' and credits in 1-3 business days. The 7labs FAQ that documents this is from 2014, so the fee/timing detail is dated; the entity and wire method are current.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/3025029 read 2026-09-17; 7labs.io wire-transfer FAQ (17 Mar 2014); webtrickz.com.

findings.finding: Indian tax on AdSense for an individual: no Indian TDS is deducted (the payer is a non-resident entity; the 'Section 194-O'-style e-commerce TDS does not apply to AdSense). Google's India tax-information page cites 'Section 393(1) of the Income Tax Act, 2025' and 'Section 52 of the CGST Act' but only for Google Play Store paid apps and in-app purchases, where Google acts as e-commerce operator; it asks for PAN and, for individuals (PAN 4th character 'P'), Aadhaar-PAN linkage. GST: AdSense is an export of services, zero-rated, but zero-rating requires filing a Letter of Undertaking (Form GST RFD-11) each year; the Rs 20 lakh aggregate-turnover threshold applies. Sources disagree on US withholding: one CA firm says Google withholds 15% US tax on AdSense with PAN submitted (that rate is the India-US treaty rate for YouTube US-viewer earnings); Google's AdSense help says US tax info is required and withholding applies to US-sourced earnings, and for AdSense-for-content the US-sourced share is normally nil. Treat as: submit the US tax form in AdSense, expect 0% on non-YouTube AdSense, and get a CA to confirm.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/product-documentation/answer/15152449 and /13401799 read 2026-09-17; guptachandanassociates.com 2026 guide; incorpx.io and taxaj.com (search summaries). The 15%-vs-0% disagreement is recorded, not resolved.

findings.finding: Web rewarded eCPMs, 2026, two vendor datasets that disagree at the top and agree at the bottom. Playgama (Head of Monetization Valeria Svistunova, quoted by Cinevva 6 Sep 2026): rewarded video 'clears roughly $15 to $28 eCPM in the United States, $8 to $15 in the EU, and just $1 to $3 in tier-3 markets like India and Brazil', gross before portal split; banners 'pennies'. AppLixir (2026): gross tier-1 (US, UK, CA, JP) $6-15, tier-2 (most of EU) $5-9, tier-3 (IN, BR, SEA) $1-4; take-home after geo blend, consent, opt-in, fill and revenue share $4-8, with a worked example degrading a '$20 benchmark' to $4.20. FatChilli (EU news sites, 2025): AdSense/Ad Manager rewarded on web at '€30+' CPM but fill 'up to 30%'. No source publishes an India-only web rewarded eCPM; the $1-4 tier-3 band is the best available.
findings.evidence: app.cinevva.com/guides/web-game-monetization (updated 6 Sep 2026); applixir.com 'Do rewarded ads actually make money on web games?' (2026); fatchillimedia.com (2025). All vendor data.

findings.finding: India display economics for entertainment/sports content: upGrowth (updated 16 Sep 2026, own estimates) puts AdSense page RPM at Rs 40-165 for 'entertainment and news' (vs Rs 250-830 finance), CPC Rs 4-16, CTR 1-3%; open-web programmatic media CPMs Rs 80-150 run-of-network and Rs 150-280 contextual. Partnerkin's 'India CPC $0.07' is 2021 data re-dated. Sports-niche RPM of $9-18 (adstimate, 2026) is a global figure dominated by tier-1 traffic. Practitioner consensus: RPM is driven by visitor geography, not by the page language.
findings.evidence: upgrowth.in AdSense-earnings-India (Feb 2026, updated Sep 2026) and programmatic-pricing-India (20 Apr 2026); partnerkin.com (Sep 2021); adstimate.com sports RPM (2026, unverified).

findings.finding: What raises eCPM/RPM, with Google's own numbers where they exist. Speed: Google/DoubleClick 'The Need for Mobile Speed' (2016, n=4.5K sites): 'publishers whose mobile sites load within 5 seconds earn up to 2X greater mobile ad revenue than those whose sites load within 19 seconds'; 5s vs 19s sites had '25% higher viewability', '70% longer average sessions', '35% lower bounce rates', '60% greater pageviews per visit'. Viewability: Google's '5 factors' study (Active View, 2014): average publisher viewability 50.2%; 'the most viewable ad position is right above the fold, not the top of the page'; 68% of above-the-fold vs 40% of below-the-fold ads viewable; vertical units most viewable (120x240 at 55.6%, 300x250 lowest at 41.0%). Ad Manager's current best practices: 'Place ads in line with the main content', vertical sizes such as 160x600 are most viewable, lazy-load below-the-fold slots, keep tags async. Lazy loading raises viewability but 'decreases impressions and revenue' if set too aggressively (practitioner reports).
findings.evidence: thinkwithgoogle.com 'Need for Mobile Speed' PDF read in full 2026-09-17; martech.org and mediapost.com reports of the 2014 study (the original Think with Google page now redirects); support.google.com/admanager/answer/6199883 read 2026-09-17; wpadvancedads.com and webmasterworld.com on lazy loading.

findings.finding: Consent and eCPM: under Google's TCF integration, if the TC string is unparseable or the user refuses Purpose 1 (device storage), 'Limited ads can serve' (no personalisation, narrower demand); TCF v2.2 strings stopped being accepted on 1 March 2026. Vendor CMPs claim Limited Ads cut eCPM 'by 50% or more' and that broken compliance dropped AdSense revenue 40-60%; no Google-published percentage exists. Blocking controls: Google says blocking categories 'removes eligible ads from competing in the ad auction' and can lower earnings; keeping Gambling & Betting blocked (decision.md) is a deliberate, priced choice.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/admanager/answer/9805023 read 2026-09-17; dataslayer.ai, cookie-script.com, applixir.com TCF posts (vendor claims); support.google.com/adsense/answer/164131 and /186376 (search summary).

findings.finding: How the incumbents monetise, from their live ads.txt files (fetched 2026-09-17). Sporcle: 564 lines, 107 distinct seller domains, ManagerDomain=mediatradecraft.com (a Google Channel Partner), updated 1 Sep 2026; CEO Ali Aydar in Google's case study: 'Programmatic ads are fundamental to our strategy, we would not exist without them'; 100 million page views a month; ad-free tier Sporcle Orange at $4/month or $44/year; founder Matt Ramme has said ads are about 90% of revenue and subscriptions the rest. JetPunk: 177 lines, 48 sellers, managerdomain=ascendeum.com, two google.com DIRECT pub IDs plus Criteo, Sonobi, MediaGrid; staff have told users the number of ads per quiz page did not change but they moved to 300x250 units because those earn more than 728x90 (message-board snippet; the page blocks fetches); a premium ad-free tier exists. Quizly.co: 173 lines / 47 sellers with its own Prebid + AdX stack. Playbuzz: 249 lines / 63 sellers. FunTrivia: 7 lines, AdSense plus Exponential/Tribal Fusion. Quizizz and Kahoot have no ads.txt at all: they are SaaS/EdTech, not ad businesses, and are the wrong comparators. Trivia Crack's web ads.txt returns AccessDenied (app-first).
findings.evidence: curl of https://<domain>/ads.txt for sporcle.com, jetpunk.com, quizly.co, playbuzz.com, funtrivia.com, quizizz.com, kahoot.com, triviacrack.com; google.com/ads/publisher/stories/sporcle; sporcle.com/blog/enjoy-sporcle-ad-free; sramanamitra.com Ramme interview part 5 (search summary, page 403); jetpunk.com message board (search snippet, page 403).

findings.finding: Where a quiz site's ad impressions come from: Sporcle's 100M monthly page views are quiz pages, i.e. the play-and-results page is the content page; the ad-free tier removes ads from the quiz page and replaces them with 'detailed statistics on the Quiz Page' for members, which tells us the ad slots on the free site sit beside the quiz and its results. JetPunk's ad discussion is about the quiz page's 300x250 units and a right rail on the front page that users complained 'cut off the quizzes' titles and thumbnails'. Neither site is reported to use interstitials or vignettes on the play flow; both run mid-tier managed programmatic (many SSPs via a manager domain) rather than plain AdSense.
findings.evidence: sporcle.com/memberships/benefits and blog (search summaries); jetpunk.com message-board snippets; ads.txt files as above. The exact slot positions could not be observed because both sites block automated page fetches.

findings.finding: H5 Games Ads reporting: 'For the rewarded format, the clicks metric captures both physical clicks and engaged views', so CTR and CPC are meaningless for rewarded placements and must be broken out by the 'Ad format' dimension (Interstitial vs Rewarded).
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/13292016 read 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: IAB 'Creative Guidelines and Best Practices in Advertising in Gaming' (March 2024): for in-game video 'three to five impressions per user per day is considered best practice to avoid ad fatigue'; 'consider a minimum of two ads concurrently, but no more than four or five to avoid interfering with gameplay. Avoid "ad stuffing" which slows down game performance'; interstitials should follow the IAB New Ad Portfolio, 'requiring a clear close button and avoiding forced countdowns'; 'in-game ads typically cover about 1.5% to 10% of screen real estate'; audio ads capped at 'one to three audio ads per 20 minutes of gameplay'. The document explicitly scopes out adjacent interstitial/banner units ('should refer to existing IAB standards') and viewability.
findings.evidence: iab.com PDF read in full (46 pages) 2026-09-17.

findings.finding: Google's own long-form publisher guide, 'The AdSense Guide to Audience Engagement' (2016, 23 pp.), contains no ad-placement heat map at all; it is about content and journeys: '61% of users would quickly move on to another site if they didn't find what they were looking for right away', 'Only 9% of users will stay on a mobile site or app if it doesn't satisfy their needs', '67% of users will switch if it takes too many steps'. The famous 'AdSense heat map' circulating on blogs is not a Google document. The guide's operative claim for us: engagement (return visits, pages per session) is the lever Google itself tells publishers to pull, which for a quiz means the results page must lead to the next quiz.
findings.evidence: services.google.com/fh/files/misc/adsenseaudienceengagement.pdf read in full 2026-09-17; adsense.googleblog.com April 2016 announcement.

findings.finding: MonetizeMore's H5 games piece (19 Sep 2024) claims 'H5 games ads have proven to improve game retention with user session times increasing 2X and ad revenue improving by 3X', unattributed; Clickio claims Ad Manager 'delivers better performance than AdSense for H5 game monetization' (vendor). MonetizeMore's AdMob playbook (2026) claims a clear value-exchange consent flow lifts rewarded opt-in 'from 35 percent to over 60 percent' and that top gaming apps take '50 to 70 percent of ad revenue from rewarded units'. Web game fill: NitroPay (23 Jul 2026) calls 85-95% healthy for display on web games and notes gaming sites see 'higher ad blocker usage than the open web'; rewarded web fill is far lower (FatChilli 'up to 30%').
findings.evidence: monetizemore.com game-monetize-online-games (2024) and admob-monetization (2026); blog.clickio.com H5; blog.nitropay.com fill-rate (2026); fatchillimedia.com. All vendor claims.

findings.finding: Network thresholds and shares for a small web publisher, 2026: AdSense 68%/80% (from lane-adtech) with no minimum beyond approval; Google Ad Manager free tier with Open Bidding/AdX only via an MCM partner, free up to 90M monthly non-video impressions in US/CA/AU/NZ, 150M elsewhere, 200M in some regions, 800K video (only non-Google demand counts); Ezoic now requires '250,000+ monthly active users' for new sites (grandfathering for sites live before 19 Feb 2026; Incubator for smaller sites); Mediavine Journey 1,000+ sessions at 70% share, Mediavine 75% after $5,000 annual revenue, rising to 80-90% at $100K-$1M+; Raptive 25,000 pageviews/month with at least 50% US/UK/CA/NZ/AU traffic, 75%; Monumetric Propel 10,000 pageviews with a $99 setup fee; Playwire 500K pageviews/month; AppLixir 5,000 DAU (both from lane-adtech). An India-majority audience is ineligible for Raptive on geography and would be the low end of every other network's yield.
findings.evidence: support.ezoic.com getting-started requirements read 2026-09-17; thisweekinblogging.com (1 Nov 2025) for Mediavine/Raptive; monetizemore.com GAM impression-limit article (updated 1 Jun 2026); Monumetric via search summary (site 404).

findings.finding: India, Google Ads side: from 21 January 2026 'all Rummy and Daily Fantasy Sports promotions targeting India will be disallowed' with the certification path removed entirely, following the 2025 Act; on the AdSense side this means the Indian gambling/RMG advertiser pool that used to bid on sports inventory during IPL is gone, so a sports-quiz site should not model any 'fantasy app' demand into IPL-season eCPMs.
findings.evidence: ppc.land (7 Jan 2026), storyboard18.com, igamingexpert.com; Google's own policy-update page lists the item but the text was not readable.

findings.finding: India, ASCI: the real-money-gaming advertising guidelines took effect 15 December 2020 and require that ads 'not be aimed at minors, not present gaming as a source of livelihood or link it to success' and carry 'a prominent disclaimer regarding the risk of financial loss and the addictive nature of such games' (commonly rendered 'This game involves an element of financial risk and may be addictive. Please play responsibly and at your own risk', at least 20% of the ad space); in the first week of IPL 2022 ASCI flagged 14 of 35 gaming ads and 285 social-media RMG ads in March alone. None of this applies to a no-money quiz, but it is the template regulators use to read a 'coins' game, so the 'coins are not money' statement should be as prominent as an ASCI disclaimer.
findings.evidence: ascionline.in press release 12 Apr 2022 read in full; exchange4media / S.S. Rana summaries for the disclaimer wording and 20% rule (likely).

findings.finding: India, the Act: PRS's summary of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 defines an online money game as one that 'involves a user paying money or other stakes in expectation of receiving monetary or other enrichment', 'other stakes' as 'credits, coins, and tokens equivalent or convertible to money', and an online social game as one 'offered solely for recreation, entertainment, or skill development'; advertising a money game carries 'imprisonment up to two years, a fine up to Rs 50 lakh, or both'; registration of online social games is an optional mechanism the central government may create, not a duty. Section 6 (per Lexology) bans any advertisement that 'directly or indirectly promotes or induces' playing a money game, on every medium. MeitY's PDF of the Act still returns 403 to automated fetches.
findings.evidence: prsindia.org billtrack read 2026-09-17; lexology.com summaries (search); meity.gov.in PDF 403.

findings.finding: India ad blocking: DoubleVerify (2026) reports 48% of Indian consumers say they use an ad blocker, 'marginally higher than the global figure of 47%'; other aggregators put India near 50% and attribute it to mobile data cost. This is self-reported and higher than GWI's measured ~30% global figure in lane-adtech; the two are not comparable and are recorded as a disagreement.
findings.evidence: medianews4u.com report of DoubleVerify data (2026); cropink.com / sqmagazine aggregators.

findings.finding: India seasonality: IPL is the annual peak for Indian digital ad rates (IPL 2025 mobile pre-roll around Rs 340 CPM, CTV Rs 650 CPM; broadcaster rates up 10-15% on TV/digital and 30% on CTV; knockouts a further 10-15%); India CTV benchmarks describe IPL (April-May) as the year's highest CPMs and the festive season (September-November) as the second peak. These are buy-side broadcaster rates, not open-web publisher yields, but they mark when open-auction demand in India is strongest. Global display seasonality (Q4 40-80% above Q1) is a US-centric pattern that India only partly follows.
findings.evidence: exchange4media.com, pitchonnet.com, themediaant.com (IPL 2025); ctv.stratpulsetechlabs.com India CTV benchmarks; newormedia.com for Q4/Q1.

findings.finding: Hindi vs English inventory: no publisher, network or Google source publishes a Hindi-vs-English eCPM for the same Indian audience. Practitioner blogs say RPM follows visitor geography rather than page language; one Hindi blogger reports a $5.41 page RPM; one guide argues English pages serving Indian users can earn less than local-language pages because Indian advertisers buy in the vernacular; India's largest vernacular ad exchange (Readwhere) exists but publishes no rates. Treat Hindi inventory as priced like Indian-geo inventory until measured.
findings.evidence: postpaisa.in (Nov 2024), ybierling.com, adpushup.com India networks (all blogs).

findings.finding: India DPDP consent mechanics beyond what lane-adtech records: consent requests must be 'clear and easy to understand', available 'in English and any of the 22 recognized Indian languages', purpose-specific, and withdrawable; the Rules give an 18-month phased window (core obligations May 2027). For AdSense this means the same CMP surface that serves TCF in the EU must show an English/Hindi consent notice in India for personalised ads, and no personalised ads at all to anyone not assured 18+.
findings.evidence: cookieyes.com DPDPA guide, india-briefing.com, ey.com DPDP Rules notes (search summaries); PIB PDF not read.

findings.finding: 'Earn' communities are the specific IVT risk for a coins game in India: the search index for 'AdSense India RPM' is dominated by sites like just2earn.com, earn4link.in and earnredeemcode.in, i.e. paid-to-click and link-shortener ecosystems. A product whose public promise is 'watch an ad to earn coins' will be shared into those channels; traffic that arrives to farm rewards across many accounts is, in Google's terms, 'third-party services that generate clicks or impressions' and will produce IVT deductions or an ad-serving limit even though each individual view is opted-in. Mitigation belongs in the reward layer (per-account caps, device velocity, no reward for datacentre/VPN ASNs) rather than in the ad layer.
findings.evidence: Inference from the Google IVT text above plus the search results returned for India RPM queries on 2026-09-17; no case study of a games site being limited for this was found.

recommendations.what: Split the product into two ad surfaces with different stacks. (1) Static SEO pages (question/answer, results-share, league tables, fixture quizzes) run AdSense Auto ads with in-page ad load capped at 3, one manual in-content responsive unit 'right above the fold' after the answer, a bottom anchor on mobile, and vignettes on link-click only. (2) The app shell (lobby, duel, receipt, practice) runs only H5 Games Ads 'reward' placements plus at most one display unit under a content-bearing receipt; Auto ads script must not be loaded in the shell at all.
recommendations.why: Vignettes now fire on back-button and 30 s inactivity+interaction (9 Feb 2026 triggers); anchors on a non-scrolling screen cover the controls; both are the H5 'interfere with user navigation' and 'interrupt continuous game play' violations. The SEO pages are ordinary content pages where all of those formats are allowed and where the incumbents (Sporcle, JetPunk) earn their money.

recommendations.what: Make the duel receipt a content screen before it carries an ad: score, both answer times, answer review with explanations, rating change, the fairness receipt, and the 'next duel' action above the ad card. Never show a display unit on a bare 'You won/lost' transition, a loading screen, an error, the login or the coin-empty alert.
recommendations.why: Publisher Policies: no ads on screens 'used for alerts, navigation or other behavioral purposes' or 'without publisher-content'. The ad card already below the duel receipt (commit 1960cd3) is compliant only while the receipt above it is substantive.

recommendations.what: Apply for AdSense with the crawlable question/answer site, not the app: first-party domain, at least the About, Contact and Privacy pages, the SEO pages indexed, HTTPS, and a real number of substantive pages, then wait for the account review (days to 2-4 weeks) before submitting the H5 Games Ads form. Noindex thin per-question pages until they carry an explanation, a source and stats.
recommendations.why: 'Low value content' / 'replicated content' is the standard refusal for templated pages; the H5 programme needs an already-approved account; 'approval is not guaranteed'.

recommendations.what: Reward copy rule, enforced in source strings: the offer may only describe the exchange ('Watch a short ad to earn 50 coins', 'Watch an ad: +1 practice drill'). Ban 'support us', 'keep the game free', 'help the developer', 'click', arrows or hands pointing at the ad, countdowns on the opt-in, and any text on the opt-in that argues for saying yes. The opt-in must have an equal-weight 'No thanks'. Label any display unit 'Advertisement'.
recommendations.why: 'Policies for ad units that offer rewards' bans text 'other than to describe the reward(s) offered' and names 'watch this ad to support our business' as the violation; 'Encouraging clicks' names 'support us' and arrows; ad labels may only be 'Advertisements' or 'Sponsored Links'.

recommendations.what: Cloudflare hygiene before applying: serve /ads.txt and the AdSense meta tag from the static-assets root of the domain; add a WAF custom rule that skips bot protection for user agents containing Mediapartners-Google, Google-Display-Ads-Bot and AdsBot-Google (or for the /ads.txt path); keep Bot Fight Mode otherwise; set sellers.json visibility to Transparent; run the AdSense crawler tester after deploy.
recommendations.why: Bot Fight Mode is documented to challenge Google's ad bots, which surfaces as ads.txt 'not found' and site-availability failures during review; sellers.json confidentiality 'might impact your revenue' per Google.

recommendations.what: Invalid-traffic discipline for a coins game: test only with data-adbreak-test='on' and never click or watch live units from staff devices; gate rewards (not ads) by per-account daily caps, device velocity and datacentre/VPN ASN checks; never buy traffic, run traffic exchanges or pay referrers per view; keep the 'earn coins' promise out of headlines in India 'earn' channels; monitor AdSense IVT deductions and any 'account being assessed' limit weekly for the first 90 days.
recommendations.why: Google lists self-clicks, encouraging clicks, paid-to-click/paid-to-surf services and bot traffic as the closure causes; new accounts commonly get a precautionary serving limit; deductions above the normal 1-5% are the early warning.

recommendations.what: Set the H5 frequency hint to the default 120s (do not lower it) and add product-side caps: one reward offer per duel outcome, a visible daily counter, 60-120 s cooldown between rewarded views; log every adBreakDone breakStatus (frequencyCapped, dismissed, ignored, viewed) as analytics events so opt-in, completion and dismissal rates are measured from day one.
recommendations.why: Google's hint is average-based and may be overridden server-side; the breakStatus values are the only completion telemetry the API gives on web; IAB gaming guidance treats 3-5 ad impressions per user per day as the fatigue ceiling for in-game video.

recommendations.what: On SEO pages: keep vignette frequency at 10 minutes or longer, turn OFF 'Allow additional triggers for vignette ads', and use the documented per-link exclusion on any link that enters the app shell so a vignette never fires between a content page and a duel.
recommendations.why: Additional triggers (end of article, inactivity, back button, tab switch) are on by default when vignettes are on and would fire on the transition into play.

recommendations.what: Performance budget as an ad-revenue lever: async ad tags only, reserved slot heights (zero CLS from ads), below-the-fold display units lazy-loaded with a conservative margin, no ad requests on the duel screen, and an India 3G/4G LCP target under 2.5 s for SEO pages.
recommendations.why: Google's own study: sites loading in 5 s vs 19 s earned up to 2x mobile ad revenue with 25% higher viewability and 70% longer sessions; over-aggressive lazy loading measurably cuts impressions.

recommendations.what: Placement inside content pages: one responsive unit immediately after the answer/explanation (just above the fold on mobile), one multiplex or 300x250 at the end before 'related questions', no unit inside the answer options, and at least 150 px between any unit and an interactive quiz element.
recommendations.why: Google 2014: 'right above the fold' is the most viewable position and 300x250 the least viewable size on its own, so pair it with a vertical/multiplex unit; the 150 px rule is Google's own recommendation for game pages; JetPunk reports 300x250 out-earning 728x90 on quiz pages.

recommendations.what: Consent surface: run Google's certified 'Privacy & messaging' CMP for EEA/UK/CH (already decided) and extend the same surface to India with an English + Hindi DPDP consent notice for personalised ads; serve non-personalised ads to anyone who declines or is not age-assured 18+, and measure the consent rate as a first-class metric.
recommendations.why: Google serves 'Limited ads' without Purpose 1 consent; vendor estimates of the eCPM loss run to 50%+ (unverified); DPDP requires purpose-specific consent in English or a scheduled language.

recommendations.what: Model India on Rs 40-165 display RPM and $1-4 gross rewarded eCPM, with a 48% self-reported ad-block rate, and time the India season calendar to IPL (April-May) and the September-November festive window when open-auction demand peaks; do not model any fantasy/RMG advertiser demand.
recommendations.why: Only published India yields for entertainment content; IPL and festive are the documented demand peaks; Google Ads removed rummy/DFS from India on 21 Jan 2026.

recommendations.what: Report rewarded and interstitial separately by the 'Ad format' dimension; never compute CTR/CPC on rewarded placements; track RPM per SEO page template and ARPDAU per geo for the shell.
recommendations.why: AdSense counts engaged views as 'clicks' for the rewarded format.

recommendations.what: Payments/tax checklist for the founder (India individual): PAN with Aadhaar linked, bank account with SWIFT that accepts USD inward remittances (purpose code P1007), address PIN within 4 months of generation, US tax form in AdSense, a CA to file the GST LUT (Form RFD-11) for zero-rated export of services and to confirm whether any US withholding applies; expect no Indian TDS.
recommendations.why: AdSense pays from Google Asia Pacific Pte Ltd Singapore by USD wire; threshold $100; sources disagree on US withholding (15% vs 0%), so it needs a professional answer.

recommendations.what: At 25,000 pageviews/month with 50%+ tier-1 traffic evaluate Raptive; at 1,000 sessions Mediavine Journey (70%) is a candidate for the SEO pages only, not the shell; at 5,000 DAU trial AppLixir for the shell's rewarded slot; move the shell to Ad Manager rewarded-for-web via an MCM partner only if H5 fill is weak.
recommendations.why: Network thresholds and shares as of Nov 2025-Sep 2026; Ezoic is closed to sites under 250,000 monthly users since 19 Feb 2026.

recommendations.what: Add a Sporcle-Orange-style ad-free membership (order of $4/month, $44/year) once ads are live, priced as the second revenue line, not the first.
recommendations.why: Sporcle: ads about 90% of revenue, subscriptions the rest; the ad-free tier is the standard second line for quiz sites.

recommendations.what: Keep the 'coins have no cash value, cannot be bought, sold, withdrawn or transferred' statement as prominent as an ASCI RMG disclaimer (visible on the wallet, the reward opt-in and the receipt), and keep all betting vocabulary out (decision.md section 3).
recommendations.why: ASCI's RMG template (prominent risk disclaimer, no minors, not a livelihood) is how Indian regulators read a 'coins' game; the Act's 'other stakes' language names coins and tokens.

risks: Loading the Auto ads script on the app shell: vignettes now trigger on back-button and 30 s inactivity+interaction and anchors cover a non-scrolling screen; this is the fastest path to an H5 policy strike and Better Ads non-compliance.
Applying for AdSense with the app shell instead of content pages, or with hundreds of templated question pages, yields a 'low value content' / 'replicated content' refusal that costs weeks per retry.

A results/receipt screen that is visually a transition ('You lost') with an ad on it is a 'screens used for alerts, navigation or other behavioral purposes' violation; the ad is compliant only when the receipt is content.

'Earn coins' communities (paid-to-click / link-shortener ecosystems that dominate India 'AdSense RPM' search results) can turn opted-in rewarded views into invalid traffic at the account level; the first symptom is an 'account being assessed' serving limit or deductions above 5%.
Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode / security level blocking Mediapartners-Google and Google-Display-Ads-Bot, producing ads.txt 'not found', failed site checks and unfilled requests.
Reward copy drift: any 'support us', 'keep it free', arrow or nudge on the opt-in is a named violation of the rewards and encouraging-clicks policies; source strings must be linted.

Web rewarded eCPM sources disagree 2x at the top (Playgama vs AppLixir); India is $1-4 gross on both, ad-block is ~48% self-reported, and display RPM for entertainment is Rs 40-165: India cannot carry the business on ads alone.

No India-specific rewarded fill data exists; FatChilli's 'up to 30%' EU fill for web rewarded suggests the reward offer will often have nothing to show (beforeReward not called), which the UI must handle gracefully (no dead 'watch ad' buttons).
Tax uncertainty: US withholding on AdSense for an Indian individual is reported as 15% by one CA firm and effectively 0% by Google's structure; GST zero-rating is lost without an LUT filed in time.

Policy churn: vignette triggers (Feb 2026), Ezoic minimums (Feb 2026), Google Ads India RMG (Jan 2026), TCF 2.3 (Mar 2026) all moved within nine months; anything in this file older than a quarter should be re-read.

Google's Publisher Policies text on 'Inventory value' and the H5 placement rules are broad; a keyword-driven manual review of a 'coins' sports game could still read the reward loop as gambling-adjacent (see lane-adtech), and AdSense strikes are account-wide across the SEO pages and the shell.
indiaSpecifics: Payment: USD wire from Google Asia Pacific Pte Ltd (Singapore) to an Indian bank with SWIFT; bank converts at its rate and may charge a conversion fee; purpose code P1007; $100 threshold; 21st-26th; PIN by post in 2-3 weeks.

Tax: no Indian TDS on AdSense; Google's Section 393(1)/CGST s.52 withholding applies to Play Store sales, not AdSense; PAN + Aadhaar linkage required for individuals; GST export-of-services zero-rating needs an annual LUT; US withholding disputed (15% vs 0%) - get a CA ruling.

Yield: entertainment/news AdSense RPM Rs 40-165 (upGrowth 2026); open-web programmatic CPM Rs 80-280; rewarded web $1-4 gross (AppLixir) / $1-3 (Playgama); no Hindi-vs-English split published; 48% self-reported ad blocking.
Seasonality: IPL (April-May) is the annual demand peak, festive September-November the second; IPL 2025 mobile CPMs around Rs 340; plan seasons and content pushes around those windows.

Demand pool: rummy and daily-fantasy advertisers were removed from Google Ads India on 21 Jan 2026; the RMG money that used to flood sports inventory in IPL is not coming back; keep 'Gambling & Betting (18+)' blocked anyway.

Consent: DPDP consent notices must be clear, purpose-specific and offered in English or any of the 22 scheduled languages; no targeted ads or profiling for under-18s; core obligations by May 2027; serve non-personalised ads to unassured users.

Regulatory reading: ASCI's RMG rules (prominent financial-risk disclaimer, no minors, not a livelihood) and the PROG Act's 'coins and tokens equivalent or convertible to money' are the lenses; the 'coins are not money' statement must be as visible as an ASCI disclaimer and the coin must stay unpurchasable and untransferable.

Invalid traffic: India's 'earn' ecosystems (paid-to-click, link shorteners) are the realistic source of reward-farming traffic; mitigate in the reward layer (account caps, device velocity, datacentre/VPN ASN checks) and never advertise the product as a way to 'earn'.
Language inventory: treat Hindi pages as Indian-geo inventory for modelling; measure RPM per language once live because no public data exists.
